title: Forms of water

match.reason: The bank point teaches the broader hydrosphere and water cycle at Year 11 depth, while the new Year 7 point is about the forms of water (salt, fresh, ice, vapour) as resources, so it is a different idea at a different depth.

draft.title: Forms of water
card: Most of Earth's water is salt water, found in the oceans. Only a small share is fresh water.
Much of the fresh water is not easy to reach. It is frozen as ice in glaciers and ice sheets, or stored underground as groundwater.
Water exists as a liquid, as ice and as water vapour, a gas in the air. Each form can become a resource when people find a use for it.
For example, groundwater can be pumped for farms, and salt water can be treated to make drinking water.
draft.remember: Most water is salty, much fresh water is ice or underground, and every form can be a resource.

a.q: Which statement about Earth's water is correct?
opts: Most of it is salt water
Most of it is fresh water
Most of it is water vapour
Most of it is groundwater
a.why: Most of Earth's water is in the oceans, and it is salty. Fresh water is only a small share, and groundwater is just part of that share.
a.clue: Think about where most of the water on Earth sits.

b.q: A town in Western Australia pumps water from deep underground to supply homes. Which statement describes this water?
opts: It is groundwater, a form of fresh water
It is salt water that has been frozen
It is water vapour taken from the air
It is ice that has melted in a glacier
b.why: Water stored underground is groundwater, and it is a form of fresh water that people can use as a resource. Ice is also fresh water, but this water is pumped from below the ground, not taken from glaciers.
b.clue: Where is the water being pumped from?

a.best: Most of it is salt water

b.best: It is groundwater, a form of fresh water

problems.detail: The stem says the water is pumped 'from deep underground', and only the right option says 'groundwater'. A student can match the words without knowing the idea. The distractors are also weak, especially 'salt water that has been frozen'.

check.summary: The facts check out and both intended answers are right. Question b is very easy, because 'underground' in the stem points straight to 'groundwater' in the right option.

proposal.title: Forms of water
card: Most of Earth's water is salt water, found in the oceans. Only a small share is fresh water.
Much of the fresh water is not easy to reach. It is frozen as ice in glaciers and ice sheets, or stored underground as groundwater. Rivers, lakes and water vapour in the air hold only a tiny share.
Water exists as a liquid, as ice and as water vapour, a gas in the air. Each form can become a resource when people find a use for it.
For example, groundwater can be pumped for farms, and salt water can be treated to make drinking water.
proposal.remember: Most water is salty, much fresh water is ice or underground, and every form can be a resource.

Most of it is groundwater

a.clue: Think about where most of the water on Earth sits.

b.q: Jack says most of Earth's fresh water sits in rivers and lakes, ready to use. Which fact shows he is wrong?
opts: Much fresh water is frozen as ice or held underground
Much fresh water is held as water vapour in clouds
Most rivers and lakes are filled with salt water
Most fresh water has already been used up by people
b.why: Much of Earth's fresh water is locked up as ice in glaciers and ice sheets, or stored underground, so it is not easy to reach. Water vapour may seem like a lot of water, but the air holds only a tiny share of fresh water.
b.clue: Where is fresh water hard for people to reach?
